item.research_question: How does varying Co content and replacing Co with Al affect the single-phase structure forming, processing behavior, and microstructural characteristics of CrFeNiMo-based high entropy alloys produced by mechanical alloying?
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying using a Retch PM400 planetary ball mill with stainless steel vials and balls (dia. 10, 15, 20 mm), 10:1 ball-to-powder ratio, 320 RPM for 30 h (HEA-FREE and HEA-Co) or 270 RPM for 30 h (HEA-Al), 2 wt.% N-heptane as process control agent, in an Ar atmosphere
item.test_conditions: XRD analysis with Cu primary radiation (λ = 1.540598 Å), scanning speed of 1 s per step, angular increment of 0.04°; EDS analysis for elemental mapping and contamination; technological characterization including free flow, tap density, slope angle, and flow rate
key_findings: A high degree of alloying and homogenization was obtained after 30 h of solid-state processing for all compositions.
XRD analysis confirmed the presence of two major phases, FCC and BCC, in all three alloys, consistent with VEC calculations.
For Al0.5CrFeNiMo, the VEC value was seven, indicating a higher abundance of BCC phases and suggesting higher strength.
In Co0.5CrFeNiMo, XRD peaks shifted to the right compared to the Co-free alloy, indicating distortion or contraction in the crystalline structure due to Co entering the lattice.
Al0.5CrFeNiMo exhibited a greater degree of crystallinity and phase stability compared to CrFeNiMo and Co0.5CrFeNiMo, with the BCC phase surpassing the FCC phase in intensity.
No oxygen contamination or impurities were detected in any of the produced HEAs after 30 h of milling.
The slope angle values for all three HEAs were in the interval of 35–41°, indicating suitability for consolidation via spark plasma sintering.
Al0.5CrFeNiMo showed improved flow properties (slope angle and free flow) compared to the other two compositions.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the phase stability to the valence electron concentration (VEC) falling within the 6.8–8 interval, predicting a mixture of FCC and BCC solid solutions. The addition of Al is noted to enhance BCC phase formation, leading to strength improvement, while Co acts as an FCC phase stabilizer. The mechanical alloying process, aided by N-heptane as a PCA, facilitates high homogenization and prevents oxidation, while the specific milling parameters (RPM, BPR) are optimized to manage the ductility and welding tendencies of the constituent elements.
item.limitations: The equipment used for chemical analysis could not confirm the presence of Carbon contamination despite using N-Heptane (approx. 84% C content) as a process control agent, as it was below the detection limit.
item.future_work: Future work will be concentrated on obtaining bulk materials to be further used as electrodes for the electro-spark deposition method, with the end goal of producing corrosion-resistant coatings for aggressive environments.
quotes: The results indicated that a high degree of alloying was obtained after 30 h of solid-state processing, with notable crystallization of two major phases FCC and BCC identified confirming the HEA phase stability calculations.
It could also be noted that the Al0.5CrFeNiMo HEA presented a greater degree of crystallinity and phase stability when compared to the CrNiFeMo and Co0.5CrFeNiMo HEAs.

Future work will be concentrated on obtaining bulk materials to be further used as electrodes for the electro-spark deposition method, with the end goal of producing corrosion-resistant coatings for aggressive environments.
